**Spiders for Rank 2 Lie Algebras**

*Greg Kuperberg*

44 pp, 6 sections.

**Abstract.** A spider is an axiomatization of the representation theory of a group, quantum group, Lie algebra, or other group or group-like object. It is also known as a spherical category, or a strict, monoidal category with a few extra properties, or by several other names. A recently useful point of view, developed by other authors, of the representation theory of sl(2) has been to present it as a spider by generators and relations. That is, one has an algebraic spider, defined by invariants of linear representations, and one identifies it as isomorphic to a combinatorial spider, given by generators and relations. We generalize this approach to the rank 2 simple Lie algebras, namely A2, B2, and G2.
